title: Growth Projections and Planning
description: Project future system growth and plan capacity upgrades to handle scaling without emergencies.

data.text: Systems that work today may fail tomorrow if you do not plan for growth. Growth projections help you build systems that scale gracefully, avoiding costly emergency upgrades and downtime.

items: **User growth**: More users means more requests, more data, and more connections.
**Feature expansion**: New features increase API calls and storage per user.
**Geographic expansion**: Serving new regions requires data centers, CDNs, and latency optimization.
**Data retention**: Longer retention policies increase database and storage requirements.
**Peak traffic increases**: Seasonal spikes (Black Friday, back-to-school) push systems beyond average loads.

data.text: Use compound growth to project resource needs over time. Future value = Current value × (1 + growth rate)^years. A 50% annual user growth rate compounds quickly.

data.title: Growth Rate Assumptions
data.text: Always state your growth assumptions clearly. If you assume 50% annual growth, explain why — perhaps based on historical data, market analysis, or business plans.
Most products do not grow linearly. They follow an S-curve: slow early growth, rapid middle expansion, and eventual saturation. Plan for the steep part of the curve, not the beginning.

data.text: In the rapid growth phase, you may need to double infrastructure every 6–12 months. Auto-scaling and modular architecture reduce the friction of these upgrades.

Good capacity planning uses three horizons. **Short-term** (0–6 months): optimize current infrastructure. **Medium-term** (6–18 months): add capacity for projected growth. **Long-term** (18+ months): re-architect systems for order-of-magnitude scale.

terms.definition: Growth calculated on the accumulated total, not just the original amount.
A growth pattern with slow start, rapid middle, and saturation phases.
Extra capacity reserved above current needs to handle spikes and growth.

data.title: Growth Planning Checklist
points: Identify growth drivers specific to your product
Use compound growth for multi-year projections
data.takeaway: Growth projections turn reactive scaling into proactive planning.

data.title: Practice Calculation
data.description: A SaaS app has 200,000 users growing at 40% annually. Current infrastructure handles 10,000 peak QPS. How many servers will be needed in 3 years, assuming each server handles 1,200 QPS?

items.question: What if growth is faster than expected?
items.answer: Use auto-scaling groups and modular architecture to absorb surprises. The cost of over-provisioning is usually less than the cost of downtime.

items.question: How do I model seasonal growth?
items.answer: Use historical data to build a seasonal model. A retail site might see 3x traffic during holidays; model this explicitly.
